description: I’m forming a team for the Space Mission Design Game challenge. I focus on creative direction, UI/UX concept design, and project coordination. Looking for teammates skilled in game development (Unity/Godot/Web), space science/aerospace, 2D/3D art, or game design. If you want to build an engaging, scientifically grounded game together, send me a message and let's team up! 🚀
summary:
Mars Crafts is a 2D pixel-art RPG and space mission simulation game developed in Unity for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Set in the year 2045, players become cadets at a space center and lead a complete robotic mission to Mars' Jezero Crater, guided by Dr. Elena Vega, their team, and ASTRID, a helpful robot assistant.

To address the challenge, the game teaches real NASA systems engineering principles through interactive gameplay. Players repair space center power systems, build a custom rover within a strict 110-credit budget and mass limit, plan orbital trajectories, and manage energy anomalies during flight and atmospheric entry. On the Martian surface, players navigate dust storms and communication blackouts within a 240-second window to scan geological targets—an ancient river delta, a mineral outcrop, and a rock sample—using specific scientific instruments.

This project is important because it transforms complex aerospace engineering concepts into an accessible, hands-on experience. By connecting design choices directly to mission outcomes, Mars Crafts inspires students and future explorers to understand that space exploration is not just about launching rockets, but about teamwork, resource management, and scientific discovery.
details:
Mars Crafts is a 2D pixel-art adventure RPG and space mission simulation game set in the year 2045. Players step into the role of a young cadet promoted to mission commander, tasked with designing, launching, and operating a robotic expedition to a region of Mars inspired by Jezero Crater. Guided by Scientific Director Dr. Elena Vega, Aerospace Engineer Mateo Rojas, Operations Specialist Luna Torres, and ASTRID (a witty robotic assistant), the player experiences a complete 7-stage mission lifecycle representing NASA's four core mission segments: Launch, Space, Ground, and User segments.

The gameplay combines top-down exploration, educational mini-games, and strategic engineering trade-offs:

  1. Space Center Preparation: Players explore the facility, interact with characters, collect loose electrical modules, and solve a power-grid mini-game to unlock the construction workshop.
  2. Modular Rover Design: Within a strict 110-credit budget and rocket payload mass limit, players configure their rover by choosing power sources (solar panels vs. RTG), batteries (60 vs. 120 units), communication antennas (direct vs. relay), wheels (standard vs. all-terrain), and scientific instruments (camera, spectrometer, and drill arm).
  3. Trajectory & Interplanetary Cruise: Players verify launcher compatibility, select an orbital launch window, launch the rocket, and manage an in-flight power consumption anomaly by temporarily throttling non-essential subsystems.
  4. Entry, Descent, and Landing (EDL): Players monitor thermal shielding and execute timed actions for supersonic parachute deployment and controlled touchdown.
  5. Surface Exploration in Jezero: Within a 240-second operational window on a 40 × 30 top-down Martian map, players drive the rover (consuming 2 energy units per second) to scan three geological targets: an ancient river delta, a mineral outcrop, and a rock sample. Dynamic events—such as a 30-second dust storm that drops solar recharge to zero and a communication blackout lasting 10 to 40 seconds depending on the antenna—test the player's engineering choices.
  6. Post-Mission Telemetry Report: An automated evaluation connects the player's workshop choices directly to mission outcomes, awarding stars, unlockable badges (Mars Crafts Commander, Efficient, No Safe Mode), and a comparison with NASA's real Perseverance rover.

Benefits and Intended Impact The primary benefit of Mars Crafts is translating dense aerospace systems engineering into intuitive, cause-and-effect gameplay. Rather than treating space exploration as simply launching a rocket, the game demonstrates that scientific discovery depends on balancing mass, power budgets, communications, and mission objectives. Its intended impact is to inspire students and aspiring engineers by demystifying real NASA mission architectures and encouraging critical thinking, iterative redesign, and scientific curiosity.

Tools, Software, and Technical Stack

  • Game Engine & Language: Developed in Unity 2D using C# for game logic, state management, resource simulation, and dialogue systems (.slnx / .csproj project architecture).
  • Orbital & Scientific Reference: Mission mechanics, EDL phases, and transfer trajectories are grounded in official NASA systems engineering documentation, Perseverance rover specifications, and reference orbital parameters validated with GMAT (General Mission Analysis Tool).
  • Art & Version Control: Custom 2D pixel-art sprites and top-down tilemaps inspired by classic adventure and colony-sim games, managed collaboratively via Git and GitHub.

Creativity and Key Design FactorsMars Crafts stands out creatively by blending the cozy, approachable aesthetics of Stardew Valley and Minicology with authentic aerospace constraints and real-time crisis management. During development, our team carefully balanced several key factors:

  • Scientific Accuracy vs. Accessibility: Simplifying complex physics—such as thin Martian atmospheric braking and orbital phase angles—into engaging 6–8 minute gameplay loops without losing educational rigor.
  • Meaningful Engineering Trade-Offs: Ensuring there is no single "perfect" rover build; for instance, equipping all three scientific instruments with solar panels fits the budget (470 kg, 99 credits) but leaves the rover vulnerable during dust storms, whereas choosing a constant-power RTG (480 kg, 97 credits) sacrifices one scientific target for uninterrupted energy.
  • Guided Learning: Using ASTRID as an active diagnostic companion that explains why a configuration fails or how to recover from safe mode, preventing player frustration while reinforcing engineering concepts.
